title: The recursive-construction conjecture for permanents of 312-avoiding matrices
statement:
Let $f_{312}(n)$ be the maximum permanent of an $n\times n$ 0-1 matrix avoiding the permutation pattern 312. Let $\mathcal{M}_n(\ast,\circ)$ be the set of $n\times n$ matrices obtained by starting with $1\times1$ identity matrices and repeatedly applying the two operations $\ast$ and $\circ$ in any order. **Recursive-construction conjecture.** For every $n\geq1$,

$$
f_{312}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{per}(A):A\in\mathcal{M}_n(\ast,\circ)\}.
$$

The conjecture concerns whether the displayed recursive operations always contain an extremal construction. The source states it as open and does not provide a proof or counterexample.
source_name: Adam Zsolt Wagner, “Constructions in combinatorics via neural networks”, arXiv:2104.14516 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.14516

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2021). “The conjecture regarding the location of the peak was disproved by Collins who showed that for paths the peak is at index approximately $\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\right)n$.”

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.37
statement: Let $T$ denote the class of all rational functions $g$ of the form \[g(z)=\sum^n_{j=1}\frac{\lambda_j}{(z-z_j)^2},\] where the constants $\lambda_j$ satisfy $\lambda_j>0$ and $\sum^n_{j=1}\lambda_j=1$. Prove (or disprove): There is a constant $C$ with the property that for each $g$ in $T$ we can find a set $S=S(g)$ with $m(S)=\pi$ such that \[\int\int_{\Delta(R)\setminus S}|g|\,dx\,dy\leq2\pi\log R+C\] for every $R$ in $(1,\infty)$. Here $\Delta(R)=\{z:|z|<R\}$. This assertion, if true, would imply that the inequality of Problem 7.36 holds with $a=1$, and thus solve the area problem of Gehring and Reich. Problems of this sort have been considered by Fuchs and MacIntyre . (A. Baernstein)
source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

title: The odd-order exact formula for replication numbers of paths
statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, and let $\rho_R(P_n)$ denote its replication number. For odd $n\geq 1$, write the upper-bound formula according to the residue class of $n$ modulo $4$. **The odd-order exact formula.** The upper bound is tight, namely

$$
\rho_R(P_n)=\begin{cases}
 n^2/4+n^2/16+3n/8+5/16,& n\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\
 n^2/4+n^2/16+3n/8+1/16,& n\equiv 3\pmod 4.
\end{cases}
$$

Computer searches determine the exact values for $n\leq 16$, and this conjecture proposes the displayed formula for all odd $n$.
source_name: Marek Szykuła and Andrzej Kisielewicz, “Rainbow Induced Subgraphs in Replication Graphs”, arXiv:1201.5340 (2012).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.5340

title: Strengthened Erdős–Gallai–Tuza conjecture for bipartite edge covers
statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph. A set of edges is **triangle-independent** if it contains at most one edge from each triangle of $G$; let $\alpha_1(G)$ be the maximum size of a triangle-independent edge set. Let $\oldtau_1_{\mathrm{B}}(G)$ be the minimum number of edges whose deletion makes $G$ bipartite.

**Strengthened Erdős–Gallai–Tuza conjecture.** For every $n$-vertex graph $G$,

$$
\alpha_1(G)+\oldtau_1_{\mathrm{B}}(G)\leq \frac{n^2}{4}.
$$

This conjecture strengthens the Erdős–Gallai–Tuza conjecture because making a graph bipartite requires deleting at least as many edges as making it triangle-free. The paper establishes the weaker bound $\alpha_1(G)+\oldtau_1_{\mathrm{B}}(G)\leq 5n^2/16$ and reports no counterexample to the conjectured inequality.
source_name: Gregory J. Puleo, “On a Conjecture of Erdős, Gallai, and Tuza”, arXiv:1311.5332 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.5332

title: Duke's conjecture on Betti number and minimum genus
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, with Betti number $\beta(G)$ and minimum genus $\gamma(G)$. **Duke's conjecture.**

$$
\beta(G) \geq 4\gamma(G)
$$

for all graphs $G$. This strengthens the general Euler-equation bound and would imply that the smallest irreducible graph for the surface $S_k$ has Betti number $4(k+1)$; bar-amalgamations of copies of $K_{3,3}$ show that the bound would be best possible.
source_name: Timothy Sun, “On Milgram's construction and the Duke embedding conjectures”, arXiv:1303.2304 (2013).

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2013). “With regards to Conjecture , all the known counterexamples are either graphs of large girth or scaffolded graphs, and they also violate Duke's conjecture.”

title: The minimum-leaf conjecture for 3-connected cubic graphs

$$
\mathrm{ml}(G)\leq\left\lceil\frac{n}{16}+\frac12\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture is presented as open; constructions in the paper are intended to show that the bound is sharp.

title: Phase transition for the distance in the random-transposition walk
statement:
For the random-transposition walk $(\sigma_t,t\ge 0)$ on the symmetric group $S_n$, let $D_t$ be the minimum number of transpositions needed to return from $\sigma_t$ to the identity. The report states that, for every $c>0$, $n^{-1}D_{cn/2}\xrightarrow{p}u(c)$, where
\[
u(c)=1-\frac{1}{c}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{k^{k-2}}{k!}(ce^{-c})^k.
\]
Moreover, $u(c)=c/2$ for $c\le 1$, $u(c)<c/2$ for $c>1$, and $u$ has no second derivative at $c=1$.

title: Does rigidity imply infinitesimal rigidity for spanning spherical codes?
statement: Let $C=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset S^{n-1}$ be a spherical code that spans the ambient space. Call $C$ rigid (or jammed) if the only continuous motions of its points that do not decrease its minimal distance are induced by continuous rotations, i.e. by paths in $SO(n)$ starting at the identity. Call $C$ infinitesimally rigid if every infinitesimal deformation is an infinitesimal rotation: for first-order changes $y_1,\ldots,y_N$, one has $\langle x_i,y_i\rangle=0$ for every $i$ and $\langle x_i,y_j\rangle+\langle x_j,y_i\rangle\le 0$ for every pair at the smallest distance, while an infinitesimal rotation has the form $y_i=\Phi x_i$ for a skew-symmetric matrix $\Phi$. Is every rigid spanning spherical code infinitesimally rigid?

title: Optimal logarithmic exponent in the periodic discrete restriction estimate for the parabola
statement:
Determine the smallest exponent $A$ for which there is a finite constant such that, whenever $\widehat h(n)=0$ for all $|n|>M$, the solution
\[
u(x,t)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\widehat h(n)e^{2\pi i(nx+n^2t)}
\]
of the periodic Schrödinger equation on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ satisfies
\[
\|u\|_{L^6(\mathbb T^2)}\lesssim (\log M)^A\|h\|_{L^2(\mathbb T)}.
\]
In particular, the report notes that Bourgain’s counterexample forces $A\geq \tfrac16$ and asks whether the endpoint value $A=\tfrac16$ is attainable.

title: Estimating the number of colors avoiding repeated triangles
statement: **Question 14.** Let $g(n)$ be the smallest number of colors necessary to edge-color $K_n$ such that there are no two vertex-disjoint color-isomorphic triangles. Estimate $g(n)$. It is not hard to show that $c\sqrt{n}\le g(n)\le n-4$ for some $c>0$. It is conjectured that $g(n)$ grows linearly in $n$, and it may even be that $g(n)=n-O(1)$. title: The excess bound conjecture for pairs of d-polytopes
statement:
Let $d\geq 4$ be an integer, and let $\mathcal{E}^d$ be the set of $(f_0,f_1)$-pairs of $d$-polytopes. For a pair $v=(p,q)$ with

$$
p\geq d+1,\qquad \frac{d}{2}p\leq q\leq \binom{p}{2},
$$

its **excess** is $2q-dp$.

**Excess bound conjecture.** If $v\notin\mathcal{E}^d$, then

$$
2q-dp\leq 4d-10.
$$

Equivalently, the set of $(f_0,f_1)$-pairs for $d$-polytopes with excess strictly larger than $3d-10$ is

$$
\mathcal{E}_{>3d-10}^d=\left\{(f_0,f_1):\frac{d}{2}f_0+\frac{3d-10}{2}<f_1\leq\binom{f_0}{2}\right\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a uniform characterization of sufficiently high-excess $(f_0,f_1)$-pairs for all dimensions $d\geq 4$, extending the preceding dimension-specific results. Its resolution would determine exactly which pairs above the threshold $3d-10$ arise from $d$-polytopes; no general proof or counterexample is supplied here.
source_name: Karim Adiprasito and Rémi Cocou Avohou, “A complete characterization of (f_0, f_1)-pairs of 6-polytopes”, arXiv:2012.14380 (2021).

title: Rudin's conjecture on squares in progressions
statement: For positive integers $N,q,a$, let $Q(N;q,a)$ be the number of perfect squares among $a,a+q,\ldots,a+(N-1)q$, and let $Q(N)=\max_{q,a\geq1}Q(N;q,a)$. Prove that $Q(N)=O(\sqrt N)$. In the stronger form, prove that $Q(N)=Q(N;24,1)$ for every $N>6$.
source_name: Combinatorics problems from Wikipedia (proposed by Walter Rudin)

title: Rational points on the non-split Cartan modular curves
statement: Show that for every prime number $p>37$, the only rational points on $X_{\\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(p)$ are the cusps and the CM-points.

title: A possible counterexample via FOM
statement: To extend the above inequality to a counterexample of Crouzeix's conjecture, one may try among other ideas to (1) find matrices $A$ where (most of) the prescribed Ritz values lie on the boundary of the field of values; (2) numerically follow the influence of the chosen prescribed residual norm $\| r_k\| $ on the max of $ p_k $ for the field of values, with prescribed Ritz values.
source_name: AimPL: Crouzeix's conjecture (posed by Jurjen Duintjer Tebbens)

title: The Borodin-Okounkov-Case-Geronimo identity is given by … Find a useful adjustment to the right-hand side so that an identity holds in the Fisher-Hartwig case.
statement:
The Borodin-Okounkov-Case-Geronimo identity is given by 

$$
\text{det}(T_N(e^f))=(e^{N\hat{f}(0)+\sum k\hat{f}(k)\hat{f}(-k)})\text{det}(1-k)
$$

 Find a useful adjustment to the right-hand side so that an identity holds in the Fisher-Hartwig case.
source_name: AimPL: Riemann-Hilbert problems, Toeplitz matrices, and applications (posed by Maurice Duits)

title: Other families of $L$-functions (problem 7)
statement: Find an exact formula for $\sum_{f\in H_k}^h L(\frac{1}{2},Sym^2f)^2$.
source_name: AimPL: Moments of zeta and correlations of divisor sums (posed by O. Balkanova)

title: Stable cohomology of character varieties
statement:
Prove (or disprove) that the cohomology of $\mathcal{U}_{G,g}$ stabilizes with respect to $g$ and compute its stable value.

A conjecture for the value of the putative stable cohomology should include Chern classes. Does it depend on anything else? What about integral cohomology?
source_name: AimPL: Motives and mapping class groups (posed by Aaron Landesman)

title: The time constant and asymptotic shape (problem 4)
statement: Assume that the edge weights $\{\omega_e\}$ are bounded and that $1/\omega_e$ has polynomial tails. Prove that $\mu({\bf e}_1)\neq0$, or find a counterexample.
source_name: AimPL: First passage percolation (posed by Jean-Christophe Mourrat)

title: Is it true that every graph whose vertices have odd degree greater than one contains a cycle of length 2^(n) for some n
statement: Erdős-Gyárfás: Is it true that every graph whose vertices have odd degree greater than one contains a cycle of length 2^(n) for some n? This one has kept me (and apparently, lots of others) up many a night trying fruitlessly to construct a counterexample. See this.
source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Erdős-Gyárfás)

title: Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups — Problem 85
statement: Find a “constructive” proof of the above theorem. More precisely, consider a ﬁnite presentation ⟨g1,.., gk|R1,.., Rm⟩ of G. Given [ ρ] ∈ D n(G) deﬁne Bn([ρ]):= inf x∈Hn max i=1,...,k d(x, ρ(gi)(x)). Find an explicit constant C, which depends on n, k, m and the lengths of the words Ri, so that the function Bn: Dn(G) →R is bounded from above by C.
source_name: Kapovich - Problems on Boundaries of Groups and Kleinian Groups (2005)

title: Soft Phases in Two-Dimensional O(N) Models
statement: Do spin correlations in the classical Heisenberg model, and other $O(N)$ models with $N>2$, decay exponentially at every nonzero temperature, or do these models have soft phases like the XY model? Prove or disprove that the low-temperature perturbative expansion is asymptotically correct, and determine whether there is a nonzero-temperature critical point and, if so, its critical indices.
source_name: Aizenman - Open Problems in Mathematical Physics (1999) (proposed by A. Patrascioiu and E. Seiler)

title: Short-Range Spin Glasses
statement: For the Edwards-Anderson Ising spin glass on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with i.i.d. mean-zero finite-variance nearest-neighbor couplings, prove or disprove the existence of a thermodynamic phase transition above a lower critical dimension $d_c$, determine $d_c$, decide whether a low-temperature phase breaks spin-flip symmetry, and characterize the number and metastate organization of pure-state pairs.
source_name: Aizenman - Open Problems in Mathematical Physics (1999) (proposed by C. M. Newman and D. L. Stein)

title: Fluctuations and efficient algorithms in first-passage percolation
statement: For i.i.d. first-passage percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, prove or disprove that boundary fluctuations have a Tracy–Widom limit and that the variance of the passage time from $0$ to $(n,0)$ has order $n^{2/3}$. Determine optimal computational bounds for finding a shortest path or estimating its length.
source_name: Benjamini - Euclidean vs. Graph Metric (proposed by Itai Benjamini)

title: Computing isomorphisms of algebraic function fields
statement: Let $F^{(1)}/k$ and $F^{(2)}/k$ be algebraic function fields of transcendence degree one and genus $g$ over a perfect constant field $k$, with $k$ algebraically closed in both fields and $g\ge 2$. Compute one or all isomorphisms $\varphi:F^{(1)}\to F^{(2)}$ that restrict to the identity on $k$. In the case $F^{(1)}=F^{(2)}=F$, this also computes $\operatorname{Aut}(F/k)$.

title: Dimensions of translated components of characteristic varieties of line arrangements
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a line arrangement in $\mathbb P^2$, and let $G=\pi_1\!\left(\mathbb P^2\setminus\bigcup_{\ell\in\mathcal A}\ell\right)$. Prove or provide a counterexample to the assertion that all positive-dimensional translated components of $V_1(G)$ have dimension one.
